newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Overseas growth cheers South African Breweries.
newsitem.headline: Overseas growth cheers South African Breweries.

text.p: South African Breweries Ltd, the world's fourth largest brewer, posted a 14 percent jump in half-year profits on Wednesday, buoyed by its fast-growing international interests.
Earnings per share in the six months to end-September rose to 185.2 cents, up from 162.5 a year ago, beating analysts forecasts of 167-182 cents.
The dividend was also increased 14 percent to 65 cents while group turnover was ahead 16 percent at 17.16 billion rand ($3.67 billion), as was attributable income at 553 million rand.
The firm's fast developing international beer division -- which extends across southern Africa, central and eastern Europe and China -- saw earnings up 26 percent.
However, the company painted a gloomy picture of domestic market conditions, warning that high interest rates would continue to undermine consumer confidence and strain disposable income.

"Notwithstanding these pressures, and providing consumer demand does not weaken significantly, the group should still achieve real growth in earnings and dividends for the year as a whole," the company said in a statement.
The firm said an unusually cold winter had not prevented growth at the firm's beer operations -- which saw earnings rise 17 percent on a modest increase in sales.
Analysts had been nervous about the results as some of SAB's operations outside its beer businesses had been showing signs of faltering.

Lower-than-expected interim earnings reports from retailer Edgars Stores, Coca-Cola bottler ABI and glass-maker Plate Glass and Shatterprufe Industries Ltd, were all seen cutting into SAB's bottomline.
SAB said a weakening in the South African economy over the period had seen private consumption spending fall and hit consumer-orientated businesses.

"Nevertheless, the extent of SAB's broadly-based consumer interests ensured that the level of turnover, aided by international expansion, exceeded 17 billion rand for the year, reflecting growth of 16 percent," the firm said.
The group's competitive markets saw margins fall across the group, but the firm said it benefitted from tight cost control and a fall in its effective tax rate.
